subject: On-prem deployment planning for EdgeWave — cluster sizing & network constraints
messages:
From: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@edgewave.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Nina Park <nina.park@edgewave.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment kickoff: network limitations + storage profile

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this — we want to run Redwood Private inside our Dublin data center and need to align on network and storage constraints before we lock cluster size. A couple of constraints up-front:

- No BGP peering with public cloud; only static routes to our on-prem border routers (MTU 9000).
- Outbound egress must traverse our central firewall (TLS inspection) and go through a proxy on 10.10.0.5:3128.
- We can provide a /23 for pod/service IPs but prefer to avoid IP overlap with our legacy infra (we run multiple VLANs).
- For storage, we have an existing NetApp NFS backend and a block iSCSI cluster; we prefer using block for model weights and NFS for logs/artifacts.

Can you share a simple checklist for cluster and node pool sizing, recommended storage classes, and any required changes to our network (eg. MTU, SNAT, LB placement) so we can present to infra? I attached our rough network diagram and storage profiles.

Thanks,
Sanjay
Sanjay Iyer
Head of Platform Engineering
EdgeWave Systems

Attachments: site-network-diagram.pdf (120KB), storage-profiles.xlsx (45KB)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@edgewave.com>
Cc: Nina Park <nina.park@edgewave.com>, Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Apr 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff: network limitations + storage profile

Hi Sanjay — appreciate the constraints. Quick read-through and next steps below. Short answer: doable, but we need alignment on 3 network items and 2 storage choices before we create the cluster blueprint.

Top network asks:
- Allocate a non-overlapping CIDR for Pods (we recommend /22 if you'll run multiple namespaces and anticipate 50+ pods per namespace). /23 is tight if you want to reserve room for autoscaling.
- Confirm MTU 9000 across the host-path and overlay stack (calico/antrea) — we'll need jumbo frames end-to-end to avoid fragmentation in RDMA/GPU hosts.
- Gateway placement: for low-latency egress to model artifacts S3-compatible store, we want the L4 load balancer (MetalLB) in the same AZ/rack as the egress NAT to avoid tromboning.

Storage recommendations (initial):
- Model weights (hot read): attach to a dedicated block storage class backed by iSCSI with iops baseline (use LVM or ZFS on the nodes if you want local cache).
- Checkpoints & artifacts: NFS backed storage class, RWX, snapshots every 6 hours.
- K8s ephemeral and kubelet eviction: set local ephemeral storage requests/limits and eviction thresholds in kubelet config to avoid pod churn during heavy GC.

I'll loop in Maya and Dev internally to draft a concrete node-pool matrix (CPU vs GPU, disk sizing, taints) and a minimal network change list.

Jonas
Jonas Weber
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-private-agent-install.md (sent on next mail)

Folks — forwarding EdgeWave constraints. Action items I propose:

1) Node pool matrix (Dev): produce two profiles: cpu-general and gpu-inference. Include CPU, mem, local-disk, and recommended persistent disk size per node.
2) Storage classes (Evelyn): define 2 SCs: block-fast (iSCSI), nfs-archive (NFS w/ snapshots) and include reclamation policies.
3) Network changes (Jonas): list minimal changes for their network team: pod CIDR recommendation, MTU checklist, MetalLB placement, and proxy egress config.

Also flag: TLS inspection + proxy will break mTLS to our control-plane certs unless they allow outbound port 443 to redwood-controls.redwood.example.com and the agent download URLs. Add that to the network ask.

Maya

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Maya Srinivasan <maya.srinivasan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Sanjay Iyer <sanjay.iyer@edgewave.com>

Subject: Re: Private deployment kickoff: network limitations + storage profile

Hi all — initial node-pool matrix below (draft). Sanjay, feel free to push back on quantities; we can do a smaller start.

Node pool: control-plane (3 nodes, m5.large-eq)
- 4 vCPU / 16Gi RAM equivalent, 200Gi root, dedicated etcd disk 100Gi (replicated)
- Not schedulable for workloads, standard taints, kubelet reserved: cpu=500m,memory=1Gi

Node pool: infra (2-3 nodes, cpu-optimized)
- 8 vCPU / 32Gi RAM, 500Gi local SSD for caching NFS (use LVM cache)
- run MetalLB speaker, coredns, ingress controller, redwood-agent

Node pool: gpu-inference (2 start, scale to 6)
- 2x A100-equivalent GPUs per node, 96Gi RAM, 4TB NVMe (local) for model cache
- Taints: gpu=true:NoSchedule; tolerations for runtime pods. Use local SSD for /var/lib/kubelet and model cache.

Storage sizing notes:
- Block-fast SC: iSCSI LUNs presented as RWO PVs, use LV-backed LUKS if they want encryption at rest. Recommend 1TB PV per GPU node for model weights cache.
- NFS-archive SC: RWX, set reclaimPolicy=Retain initially. Snapshot schedule: 6h incremental.

Network notes (summary):
- Use Calico in policy-only mode; BGP disabled (static routes). Enable MTU 9000 in CNI config.
- MetalLB in layer2 mode with speaker on infra nodes; place speakers in the same rack as egress NAT.
- Configure proxy env for nodes and agent pods: HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY and NO_PROXY for cluster internal CIDRs.

Sanjay — if you confirm MTU across the path and can provide a /22 for pods (or accept a CNI with smaller per-node IPs and IPAM), we'll produce a final BOM and Ansible playbook for provisioning.

- Dev
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Sanjay / Nina — thanks for the quick answers on the call earlier. Summary and next steps below (we'll include these in the formal plan):

Summary of confirmed decisions:
- EdgeWave will provide a dedicated /22 for pods and services; they will reserve a disjoint VLAN to avoid overlap.
- MTU 9000 is enabled end-to-end for the racks hosting GPU nodes.
- Egress will go through their proxy; EdgeWave infra will allow outbound 443 to redwood-controls.redwood.example.com and download endpoints.
- NetApp NFS kept for artifacts; iSCSI block used for model hot storage.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Dev: finalize node-pool YAMLs and resource requests, include kubelet eviction profiles (ETA 48h).
- Evelyn: produce storageclass manifests with reclaimPolicy=Retain for first week and snapshot classes (ETA 48h).
- Jonas: produce minimal network change list and MetalLB placement diagram (ETA 24h).

I'll attach the draft redwood-private-agent-install.md and the updated BOM to the HubSpot deal record. Once you sign off, we will schedule the initial infra window and provide the Ansible playbook for provisioning.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this running.

Jonas Weber
